Hitler Disagrees with Ellen Pao's Governance of a Certain Site

In order to stop giving certain websites traffic, I've seen recommendations to use Archive.is or similar pages. Is Archive.is superior to sites like Donotlink.com because they don't give any pageviews to that domain as opposed to simply denying better indexing in seach engines?
Donotlink vs Archive - what's the difference?

I wish someone had replied to you, but since no one has, I'll give you my take.

I don't think it really makes a difference which archiving service you use, frankly. The primary purpose it serves (IMO) is to create a static version of what you're linking to. People on sites like this have a habit of deleting content when they realize it's getting the wrong kind of attention. Second to that, it adds a layer by which traffic can be denied to the site being archived if you don't want to give them that kind of support (they get a hit when you make the archive, but not all the hits of the people looking at it). Mind you, the archives themselves will usually have links to the source, so users can still click through to them.

With all that said, if I had to choose between the two you mentioned, I would choose archive.is simply for its name value, meaning it's less likely someone won't go there because they don't recognize donotlink.com (I had never heard of it until this post).
